title: WPSS/506/2008 of SMT. RADHIKA DEVI Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
1
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
MCC No.661 of 2011 (Review Petition)
(On behalf of the respondents)
And
CLMA No.9117 of 2011 (Delay Condonation Application)
Along with
CLMA No.9118 of 2011 (Review Application)
(On behalf of the respondents)
In
Writ Petition (S/S) No. 506 of 2008
Gopal Singh (since deceased)
Now through his widowSmt. Radhika Devi
(substituted vide order dated 03.03.2016)
....Petitioner
Versus
State of Uttarakhand and others
...Respondents
Present: Mr.ShashankUpadhayaya, Advocate for the petitioner.
Mr. G.S. Negi, Brief Holder for the State.
Coram: Hon'bleSudhanshu Dhulia, J.
Hon'bleAlok Kumar Verma, J.
By the Court
As pointed out by the Registry,there is a delay of
354 days in filing of this review petition (CLMA No. 9118 of
2011). The review petition is on behalf of the State

2
Government.Purely in the interest of justice, we condone the
delay in filing of the review petition.
2. The review petition has been filed by the State
Government with a prayer that the order dated 05.08.2010
passed by this Court in the above writ petition be reviewed. The
petitioner (i.e. Gopal Singh), before being absorbed formally in
regular service had put in considerable long years of service in
the work charge establishment, and the question before the
Court was whether his service rendered in the work charge
establishment are liable to be counted for his pensionary
benefits. Vide order dated 05.08.2010 in the above writ petition,
it was held by a learned Single Judge of this Court that the
period of service the petitioner (Gopal Singh) had put in as a
work charge employee are liable to be counted as qualifying
service for his pensionary benefits and hence he is liable to be
given pension, which was wrongly denied to him.
3. The order of the learned Single Judge of this Court
dated 05.08.2010, it must be stated, was based on an earlier
Division Bench judgment of this Court passed in Special Appeal
No. 225 of 2008 (State of U.P. and another vs.
PitamberDuttSanwal) decided on 27.04.2010, where under
similar circumstances, the Division Bench of this Court had held
that the period of service undergone by an employee as a work
charge employee is liable to be calculated for his pensionary
benefits.
4. All the same, the order dated 05.08.2010 was
never complied by the employer of the petitioner or the State
Authorities. Instead a review petition has been filed before this
Court on 01.09.2011. The main reason for filing the review
petition is that the validity of the Division Bench order dated

3
27.04.2010 (State of U.P. and another vs.
PitamberDuttSanwal), was meanwhile referred to a larger
Bench by the Court. The larger Bench gave its decision on
06.01.2011* holding that the period of service put inby a work
charge employee cannot be calculated for his pensionary
benefits. Consequent to this decision, the review petition was
filed with a prayer that now since the larger Bench decision has
come, the order dated 05.08.2010 passed in the aforesaid writ
petition must be reviewed in the light of the new decision. The
Full Bench gave its findings based on its interpretation of Civil
Service Regulations as applicable in the State of Uttarakhand
and a Government Order dated 01.07.1989 of the erstwhile
State of Uttar Pradesh, which was also applicable in the State of
Uttarakhand.
5. Although the Full Bench in its judgment has
referred to a number of provisions of the Civil Service
Regulations, three of these would be extremely relevant here.
There are Article 361, 368 and 370 of the Civil Service
Regulations. These are as under:-
"361. The service of an officer does not
qualify for pension unless it conforms to the
following three conditions:-
First- The service must be under
Government.
Second -The employment must be
substantive and permanent.
Third -The service must be paid by
Government
(These three conditions are fully explained in
the following section)"
* Writ Petition No. 284 of 2004 (S/B), Madan Mohan Chaudhary vs. State of
Uttarakhand& others, decided on 06.01.2011, reported in 2011 (1) U.D., 6.

4
"368. Service does not qualify unless the
officer holds a substantive office on a
permanent establishment."
* * *
"370. Continuous temporary or officiating
service under the Government of Uttar
Pradesh followed without interruption by
confirmation in the same or any other post
shall qualify except-
(i) periods of temporary or officiating service
in a non-pensionable establishment,
(ii) periods of service in a work-charged
establishment, and
(iii) periods of service in a post paid from
contingencies."
6. After reading the above provisions, the Full Bench
held as under:-
"A perusal of Article 361 read with Article 368
and 370 of the CSR clearly indicates that the
service does not qualify unless the officer
holds a substantive office on a permanent
establishment and that the period of service
in a workcharged establishment will not
qualify service for the purpose of pension.
The underlying reason is that a workcharged
employee is not holding a substantive post on
a permanent establishment."
7. The Government Order dated 01.07.1989, which
was earlier interpreted in favour of the work charge employees
was now interpreted in the light of the CSR and the Full Bench
held that the service rendered by an employee in a work
charge establishment cannot be counted for his pensionary
benefits. The Full Bench said in paragraph 8 to 13 of its
judgment as under:-

5
"8. The genesis of receiving a pension is
indicated in Article 361 of the CSR. One such
condition is that the employment must be
substantive and permanent which is reiterated in
Article 368 of the CSR. Article 370(ii) excludes
periods of service spent in a workcharged
establishment for the purpose of calculating the
qualifying service.
The Government Order dated 01.07.1989
talks about temporary employees in a Government
Service retiring without being made permanent,
and are therefore not getting pensionary benefits in
view of Article 368 of the CSR, which requires an
employee to hold a permanent post. Para 2 of the
aforesaid G.O. indicates that such Government
employee, namely, temporary employees, who
have worked for a minimum period of 10 years in a
regular service, would be given pensionary
benefits in the same manner as given to a
permanent employee. A temporary employee,
even though temporary is working on a substantive
post, though not permanent. In this light, the
Government thought fit to include temporary
employees for the purpose of receiving pensionary
benefits. A workcharged employee is notworking
on a substantive post and is specifically excluded
under clause (ii) of Article 370 of the CSR.
Consequently, the period rendered in a work-charged establishment cannot be included for
claiming pension. Sub rule (8) of Rule 3 of the U.P.
Retirement Benefit Rules, 1961, supports this view.
Said sub rule defines qualifying service with the
note that if a person serves in a pensionable job,
then in work-charge establishment, and again

6
there after in regular service, such interruption
would not be disqualification. Similar provision is
contained in Article 422 of the CSR.
9) On behalf of the writ petitioner/respondent
reference is made to Rule 2 of Temporary
Government Servant (Termination of Service)
Rules 1975, which defines 'temporary service'.
According to said Rule 2, 'temporary service'
means officiating or substantive service on a
temporary post or officiating service on a
permanent post under the Uttar Pradesh
Government. These rules of 1975, are not
applicable to the work-charged employees. Clause
(d) of Rule 4 of Temporary Government Servant
(Termination of Service) Rules 1975, provides that
these rules are not applicable to the employees
serving in a work-charge establishment. In our
opinion, service rendered in work-charge
establishment, before regularization is not a
temporary service for the purposes of regular
service. It is relevant to mention here that without
there being a post, a person cannot hold it either
as a temporary employee or permanent employee.
In Para 4 of State of Himachal Pradesh Vs.
Suresh Kumer (1996) 8 Supreme Court Cases
562, it is observed by the Apex Court that work-charge employees perform the duties of transitory
and urgent nature so long as the work exists (in a
particular project). In our opinion, only because a
work-charge employee was engaged in one after
another projects does not make his services
regular without there being a permanent post.
10) In State of Mysore Vs. S.V.
Narayanappa, A.I.R. 1967 S.C.1071: (1967) 1

7
SCR 128, the Apex Court has held that the word
"Regular" or "Regularization" does not mean
"permanence". Even after regularization,
confirmation may be needed in the service. This
view was again reiterated by the Apex Court in
B.N. NagrajanVs. State of Karnataka, AI.R. 1979
S.C. 1676: (1979) 4 S.C.C. 507. That being so, in
our opinion, word "NIYAMIT" (regular) used in the
government Order dated 01.07.1989 only refers to
the temporary employees inregular service, yet to
be confirmed.
11. Para 669 of Financial Hand Book,
Volume VI provides that members of workcharged
establishment are not entitled to pension except
the conditions mentioned therein like in the case of
getting injured in the accidents etc.
12. In our considered opinion, the
Government Order dated 01.07.1989 recognizes
only status of a temporary employee on regular
post as that of a confirmed employee, for the
purposes of pensionary benefits, as is apparent
from Para 1 of the Government Order quoted
above, in which it is mentioned that many
temporary government employees get retired
without their services getting confirmed, and they
get deprived of pension due to non-confirmation on
account of condition mentioned in Article 368 of
CSR. To remove the difficulty of such temporary
employees they are treated as a confirmed
employees by the Government for the purposes of
pension. The Government Order nowhere says
that it is applicable to workcharged employees who
are neither temporary government servants, nor
permanent employees. The Government Order

8
dated 1st July 1989, nowhere interferes with Clause
(ii) of Article 370 of CSR, quoted above.
13. For the reasons as discussed above, we
answer the question referred by the Division
Bench, in negative, and the view taken by the
Division Bench of this court in Special Appeal No.
225 of 2010, (State of U.P. and another Vs.
PitamberDuttSanwal) (arisen out of Writ Petition
No. 843 (S/S) of 2003), in our opinion, is not based
on correct interpretation of law."
8. The benefit of Government Order dated
01.07.1989 (which said that the period of service of temporary
Government servant are liable to be counted for pensionary
benefits), was not given to the employees of the work charge
establishment in terms of specific bar against in C.S.R. 370. We
have now been asked to review the order dated 05.08.2010, in
the light of the findings of the Full Bench, stated above.
9. Before we come down to the merits of the review
petition in light of the subsequent orders of this Court, we must
note down the bare facts of the present case. The petitioner
(Gopal Singh) had filed this writ petition before this Court with a
case that he had worked as an employee in the work charge
establishment of Civil Construction Division II, Dhalipurfrom
01.04.1974 to 30.11.2006. Initially after putting more than 23
years of service in the work charge establishment as a Peon
(Chowkidar), he was regularised in service on 24.06.1997. He
then continued to work as a regular employee thereafter, till he
reached the age of superannuation on 30.11.2006 and retired
from service. By 30.11.2006, he had already put in more than
32 years of service in the department, out of which, 9 years and
5 months were as a regular employee. He was still denied his

9
pensionary benefits, and this was done by the State in view of
the Government Order dated 01.07.1989, which, inter alia, said
that a government employee is only eligible for pensionary
benefits if he has put in a minimum of 10 years of service as a
regular employee. Since the services of the petitioner Gopal
Singh were short by 7 months as a regular employee, he was
denied pensionary benefits. His 32 years of service in the same
establishment where he did the same nature of job throughout
were of no consequence, according to the Government
Department.
10. Meanwhile, the petitioner Gopal Singh passed
away on 12.12.2011. Later a substitution application was filed
by the wife of the petitioner Gopal Singh, which was allowed by
this Court on 03.03.2016, and thereafter the wife of Gopal Singh
i.e. the present petitioner Smt. Radhika Devi was substituted as
petitioner in the writ petition, who is before us now.
11. Being denied of his pensionary benefits, the
petitioner was constrained to file the above writ petition before
this Court, which, as we have already stated, was allowed by a
learned Single Judge of this Court vide order dated 05.08.2010
directing that the pension along with its arrears be given with
8% interest! But the petitioner was never given his pensionary
benefits, in spite of the order of this Court. The State also did
not file any appeal against the said order. Meanwhile, the
petitioner passed away in the year 2011 and he was substituted
by his wife Smt. Radhika Devi in the writ petition, who continues
to wait for her pension, even after about 14 years since the
retirement of her husband, ten years since the order of this
Court and about 9 years since his death. The circumstances
under which this review petition was filed have been stated by
us in the preceding paragraphs. This review petition, we must

10
also make it clear, had earlier come before a learned Single
Judge, but the learned Judge was of the opinion that it should
now be heard by a Division Bench, hence, by orders of the
Hon'ble Chief Justice, the Court has been nominated to hear
this review petition.
12. This review petition, however, must not only be
examined in the light of the Full Bench decision of this Court but
two decisions of the Hon'ble Apex Court which have come after
the Full Bench decision of this Court. The first is the case of
Habib Khan vs. State of Uttarakhand& others,reported in
(2019) 10 SCC 542, and the second is Prem Singh vs. State
of Uttar Pradesh and others, reported in (2019) 10 SCC 516,
which is a three Judge decision. In both these cases, it has
been held, that a work charge employee is liable for pensionary
benefits and the period of service he has given to the
department as a work charge employee is liable to be
calculated for his pensionary benefits. These two judgments of
the Hon'ble Apex Court refer to a Full Bench judgment of
Punjab and Haryana High Court, which is Kesar Chand vs.
State of Punjab and others,reported in AIR 1988 Pg 265,
where the Full Bench of Punjab and Haryana High Court had
examined the same aspect, which is, whether a work charge
employee is entitled for pensionary benefits? It came to the
conclusion that he is indeed entitled. The Rules before the Full
Bench of Punjab and Haryana High Court were of the State of
Punjab, which have been held to be in paramateriato the Rules
applicable in Uttarakhand and Uttar Pradesh. Both the above
referred judgments of the Hon'ble Apex Court have given their
approval to the correctness of the findings of the Full Bench in
Kesar Chand case of Punjab and Haryana High Court.
13. The fact of Habib Khan v. State of Uttarakhand
and others reported in (2019) 10 SCC 542 is additionally

11
relevant for our purposes since this case went before the
Hon'ble Apex Court from the High Court of Uttarakhand and it
has a similar trajectory of facts as in the present review petition
before this Court. The petitioner i.e. Habib Khan, who had put in
considerable period of service as a work-charged employee in
Government Service in Uttarakhand, and had the same Rules
governed his service as the petitioner in the present writ
petition, was also denied his pensionary benefits. He then filed
a claim petition before the State Public Services Tribunal and
the State Public Services Tribunal held that the period of service
Habib Khan had put in as a work-charged employee are liable
to be counted as qualifying service for the purposes of his
pension. Against the order of the State Public Services Tribunal,
the State filed a writ petition (i.e. Writ Petition (S/B) No. 284 of
2004), which was dismissed by the Uttarakhand High Court and
the SLP of the State before the Hon'ble Apex Court against the
said order was also dismissed. Meanwhile, a Full Bench of
Uttarakhand High Court* took a view that the period of work-charge service cannot be counted for computation of period of
qualifying service and on the basis of the said decision of the
Full Bench of Uttarakhand High Court, the order of the High
Court, dismissing State's writ petition was sought to be
reviewed. The review petition was allowed by the HighCourt
vide its order dated 26.05.2015, holding that in view of the Full
Bench decision of this Court services rendered by a work-charged employee are not liable to be counted for pensionary
benefits. In Habib Khan both the orders ofthe High Court i.e.
dated 26.05.2015 and dated 06.01.2011 of the Full Bench were
examined, we have already referred earlier. The Hon'ble Apex
Court while deciding the said case took notice of a judgment of
the Full Bench of the Punjab and Haryana High Court, which
had struckdown the parimateria provisions in the Civil Service
* Madan Mohan Chaudhary vs. State of Uttarakhand& others, reported in 2011 (1)
U.D., 6

12
Rules, which denied a work-charged employee pensionary
benefits, an order which was upheld by the Hon'ble Apex Court.
Allowing the appeal of Habib Khan, which had arose from this
High Court, the Hon'ble Apex Court stated as under:-
"4. Having recalled the facts
germane to a consideration of the case, the
question of law arising may now be adverted
to.
5. The aforesaid question is no
longer res integra in view of the facts
enumerated herein after. The relevant
provisions under which the period of work-charged service is not to be counted for
computation of "qualifying service" in the
State of Uttarakhand is Regulation 370 of
the Civil Services Regulations which is
extracted below:
"370. Continuous temporary or
officiating service under the Government of
Uttar Pradesh followed without interruption
by confirmation in the same or any other
post shall qualify except -
(i) periods of temporary or
officiating service in a non-pensionable establishment;
(ii) periods of service in a work-charged establishment; and
(iii) periods of service in a post paid
from contingencies."
6. The parimateria provision
contained in Rule 3.17 (ii) of the Punjab Civil
Services Rules had been struck down by a
Full Bench decision of the Punjab and

13
Haryana High Court in Kesar Chand v. State
of Punjab (AIR 1988 P&H 265). The
challenge by the State against the aforesaid
decision of the Full Bench of the Punjab and
Haryana High Court was negatived (Dakshin
Haryana BijliVitran Nigam v. Bachan Singh,
(2009) 14 SCC 793) by this Court. The
matter came up for consideration before this
Court, once again, in Punjab SEB v. Narata
Singh (2010) 4 SCC 317. While dealing with
the said question this Court in Para 25 of the
report held that the Full Bench decision of
the Punjab and Haryana High Court was
perfectly justified in striking down Rule
3.17(ii) of the Punjab Civil Services Rules
resulting in obliteration of the distinction
made in the said Rules between "temporary
and officiating service" and "work-charged
service". On the said basis, the Court took
the view that the period of work-charged
service should be reckoned for purposes of
computation of "qualifying service" for grant
of pension.
7. As already observed, the provisions of
Regulation 370 of the Civil Services
Regulations applicable to the State of
Uttarakhand are parimateria with the
provisions of Rule 3.17 (ii) of the Punjab
Civil Services Rules, discussed above. If
that is so, we do not see as to why the
period of service rendered on work-charged
basis by the appellants should not be
counted for purposes of computation of
"qualifying service" for grant of pension. The

14
parimateria provisions of Rule 3.17 (ii) of the
Punjab Civil Services Rules having been
interpreted and understood in the above
manner by this Court in Narata Singh
(Pubjab SEB v. Narata Singh, (2010) 4 SCC
317 we do not find any room for taking any
other view except to hold that the appellants
are entitled to reckon the period of work-charged service for the purposes of
computation of "qualifying service" for grant
of pension. We order accordingly; allow
these appeals and set aside the impugned
orders passed by the High Court.
8. All necessary and consequential
benefit in terms of the present order will be
paid and granted by the State to the
appellants forthwith and without any delay."
14. Immediately thereafter another decision came
from a three-Judges Bench of the Hon'ble Apex Court also
related to work-charged employees of State of Uttar Pradesh
and the question again was whether their services were liable
to be counted as qualifying service for pensionary benefit or
not. As case was from Uttar Pradesh, we must also bring on
record that the Rules and Regulations pertaining to qualifying
service and what service is liable to be qualified as qualifying
service for pensionary benefits as applicable to the State of
Uttar Pradesh continue to be applicable in the State of
Uttarakhand as well.
15. The Hon'ble Apex Court in the above case had
observed that employees who are actually appointed as work-charged employees and are supposed to be appointed only
for a project, however, continue in service like other regular

15
employees, and their employment is sudden project based
employment. The Hon'ble Apex Court came to the conclusion
that the very concept of work-charged employee has been
misused "offering the employment on exploitative terms for
the work which is regular and perennial in nature".Quite
similarly we also find that the initial appointment of petitioner
in the case at hand, was as a peon in the year 1974. He
continued to work as a peon in the work charge establishment
till 1997 when he was regularised in service and thereafter
retired in the year 2006. Throughout this period, he worked as
a peon. The Hon'ble Apex Court then in Prem Singh case
(supra) stated as under:
"31. In the aforesaid facts and
circumstances, it was unfair on the part of
the State Government and its officials to
take work from the employees on the work-charged basis. They ought to have resorted
to an appointment on regular basis. The
taking of work on the work-charged basis for
long amounts to adopting the exploitative
device. Later on, though their services have
been regularised. However, the period spent
by them in the work-charged establishment
has not been counted towards the qualifying
service. Thus, they have not only been
deprived of their due emoluments during the
period they served on less salary in work-charged establishment but have also been
deprived of counting of the period for
pensionary benefits as if no services had
been rendered by them. The State has been
benefitted by the services rendered by them
in the heydays of their life on less salary in
work-charged establishment.

16
32. In view of the Note appended to
Rule 3(8) of the 1961 Rules, there is a
provision to count service spent on work-charged, contingencies or non-pensionable
service, in case, a person has rendered
such service in a given between period of
two temporary appointments in the
pensionable establishment or has rendered
such service in the interregnum two periods
of temporary and permanent employment.
The work-charged service can be counted
as qualifying service for pension in the
aforesaid exigencies.
33. The question arises whether the
imposition of rider that such service to be
counted has to be rendered in-between two
spells of temporary or temporary and
permanent service is legal and proper. We
find that once regularisation had been made
on vacant posts, though the employee had
not served prior to that on temporary basis,
considering the nature of appointment,
though it was not a regular appointment it
was made on monthly salary and thereafter
in the pay scale of work-charged
establishment the efficiency bar was
permitted to be crossed. It would be highly
discriminatory and irrational because of the
rider contained in the Note to Rule 3 (8) of
the 1961 Rules, not to count such service
particularly, when it can be counted, in case
such service is sandwiched between two
temporary or in-between temporary and
permanent services. There is no rhyme or

17
reason not to count the service of work-charged period in case it has been rendered
before regularisation. In our opinion, an
impermissible classification has been made
under Rule 3(8). It would be highly unjust,
impermissible and irrational to deprive such
employees benefit of the qualifying service.
Service of work-charged period remains the
same for all the employees, once it is to be
counted for one class, it has to be counted
for all to prevent discrimination. The
classification cannot be done on the
irrational basis and when respondents are
themselves counting period spent in such
service, it would be highly discriminatory not
to count the service on the basis of flimsy
classification. The rider put on that work-charged service should have preceded by
temporary capacity is discriminatory and
irrational and creates an impermissible
classification.
34. As it would be unjust, illegal and
impermissible to make aforesaid
classification to make Rule 3(8) valid and
non-discriminatory, we have to read down
the provisions of Rule 3(8) and hold that
services rendered even prior to
regularisation in the capacity of work-charged employees, contingency paid fund
employees or non-pensionable
establishment shall also be counted towards
the qualifying service even if such service is
not preceded by temporary or regular
appointment in a pensionable establishment.

18
35. In view of the Note appended to
Rule 3(8), which we have read down, the
provision contained in Regulation 370 of the
Civil Services Regulations has to be struck
down as also the instructions contained in
Para 669 of the Financial Handbook.
36. There are some of the
employees who have not been regularised
in spite of having rendered the services for
30-40 or more years whereas they have
been superannuated. As they have worked
in the work-charged establishment, not
against any particular project, their services
ought to have been regularised under the
Government instructions and even as per
the decision of this Court in State of
Karnataka v. Umadevi(2006) 4 SCC 1. This
Court in the said decision has laid down that
in case services have been rendered for
more than ten years without the cover of the
Court's order, as one-time measure, the
services be regularised of such employees.
In the facts of the case, those employees
who have worked for ten years or more
should have been regularised. It would not
be proper to regulate them for consideration
of regularisation as others have been
regularised, we direct that their services be
treated as a regular one. However, it is
made clear that they shall not be entitled to
claiming any dues of difference in wages
had they been continued in service regularly
before attaining the age of superannuation.
They shall be entitled to receive the pension

19
as if they have retired from the regular
establishment and the services rendered by
them right from the day they entered the
work-charged establishment shall be
counted as qualifying service for purpose of
pension."
16. In view of the above two decisions, the matter
before us is no more res integra. A work charge employee is
liable to get pensionary benefits. In fact, now in view of the
above two decisions of the Hon'ble Apex Court, which came
after the filing of the review petition, the learned State
Counsel Sri Ganga Singh Negi also very fairly admits that the
pension is now liable to be given to the petitioner. The only
question is whether the arrears of only last three years are
liable to be given as this was so done in Prem Singh's (supra)
case by the Hon'ble Apex Court.
17. After hearing the facts of the present case in
detail, it is our considered opinion that the three years period
was peculiar to the circumstances in Prem Singh's case. The
facts of the present case are entirely different. In this case,
the writ petition of the petitioner was allowed by a learned
Single Judge of this Court vide order dated 05.08.2010.
Thereafter, the petitioner passed away after one year and a
review petition was filed by the State denying him pensionary
benefits for the last ten years. The petitioner and his family
have been denied his pensionary benefits for more than 10
years. Before us now is the petitioner's widow, who has not
received any amount as pensionary benefits for the last more
than ten years. Under these circumstances, we are of the
opinion that it would not be proper to limit the arrears for only
three years. In any case, there were a large number of such
cases pertaining to Uttar Pradesh and it was the case of the
Government that this may cause a financial burden on the

20
Government. This is not the case before us in the review
petition. Moreover, no such limitation on arrears was set up by
the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Habib Khan (supra)
which was from the State of Uttarakhand and had similar set
of facts as the present case. Therefore the limitation of three
years set up in Prem Singh's case was peculiar for the facts
of that case.
18. We therefore dismiss the review petition. We also
make it clear that we are in a writ jurisdiction as this review
petition has been filed for review of an order, which was
passed in a writ jurisdiction of this Court. This Court is also a
Court of equity. Though we cannot go beyond the scope of
the judgment which has already been given in favour of the
petitioner, but we must reproduce here what the learned
Single Judge in his order (dated 05.08.2010) had given to the
petitioner. The operative portion of the judgment reads as
under:-
"Accordingly, it is just and appropriate to
direct the respondents to pay the petitioner all
remaining retiral benefits, including pension within
a period of one month from the date of receipt of a
certified copy of this order. The petitioner shall be
also entitled to interest on the aforesaid arrears
payable to him at the rate of 8% from the date the
same became due to him till the date the same
are paid to him."
19. This must be done now within one month from the
date a certified copy of the order is produced before the
concerned authority, failing which the arrears shall carry an
interest of 12 per cent per annum, after a period of one
month.
(Alok Kumar Verma, J.) (Sudhanshu Dhulia, J.)
23.09.2020
Avneet/
